reranked_evidence.title: Sex Workers Struggle as COVID-19 Pandemic Continues - Reporting Texas ★ Reporting Texas
reranked_evidence.snippet: Bars, strip clubs and brothels have been shut down as non-essential businesses across the country closed for the coronavirus pandemic, leaving many sex workers out of a job. “It has completely stopped business,” said Mistress Natalie King, a dominatrix in New York City. King has been working as a professional dominatrix for more than 25 years. In light of the COVID-19 pandemic and the implementation of social distancing, King has seen a drastic decrease in in-person business and like many sex workers, she has been excluded from government financial support. “I have a corporation; I have a clothing company, a video production company and a rental space,” said Sinclaire, “None of them on paper say ‘adult,’ so my accountant just told me to apply for all of them. “I stopped doing [online work] in 2009, and I pulled back on video production, because I didn’t like dealing with the piracy,” Sinclaire said, “I haven’t really navigated it much for a while, but now I have to… That’s helped, but with three overheads, it’s been a lot.”.
